daily_reality.typical_schedule: 40-hour work week during school hours, following traditional 10-month school year schedule
daily_tasks: Prepare lesson plans in accordance with IEPs and functional abilities/needs of students
Provide adapted physical education services to students with intellectual disabilities, autism, traumatic brain injury, orthopedic impairments, or other disabling conditions
Instruct students using adapted PE techniques to improve physical fitness, gross motor skills, perceptual motor skills, or sports/game achievement
Maintain thorough student records to document attendance, participation, or progress, ensuring confidentiality
weekly_monthly_tasks: Write or modify IEPs for students with intellectual or physical disabilities
Communicate behavioral observations and student progress reports to students, parents, teachers, or administrators
Write reports to summarize student performance, social growth, or physical development
Advise education professionals of students' physical abilities/disabilities and accommodations required

regulatory.federal_mandate: IDEA Federal Regulations (300.108) requires physical education services, specially designed if necessary, must be made available to every child with a disability receiving FAPE
regulatory.certification_landscape: Only 14 states have specific endorsement/certification in adapted physical education (California, New York, Connecticut among them); 36 states have yet to address APE teacher qualifications

state_examples.california: Requires valid prerequisite teaching credential authorizing teaching of physical education K-12 or credential authorizing instruction/services in special education
state_examples.washington: References WAC 392-172A-02090(i) regarding special education qualifications; specialty endorsement provides professional recognition

regulatory.national_standards: NCPERID created national standards and voluntary national certification exam (APENS) with fifteen standards
regulatory.iep_requirements: If specially designed PE is required, services must be stated in IEP, delivered in LRE, and provided by qualified teacher

tools.assessment_focus: All PE evaluations should be individualized and examine: Participation, Fitness, Gross Motor Skills, Motor Pattern Development

automation_potential.reason: Requires complex problem-solving, creativity, strong interpersonal skills, high degree of manual dexterity

tasks_being_automated.description: AI assists with lesson planning, equipment management, attendance tracking
Smart wearable AI devices for real-time health monitoring, injury prevention, personalized training
AI algorithms analyze students' motor activity in real time and provide immediate corrective feedback

automation_potential.emerging_technologies: VR, AR, gamification create interactive learning environments particularly helpful for students with learning difficulties
automation_potential.future_outlook: AI complements rather than replaces specialists; specialists create personalized fitness plans through data analytics; specialized certifications in AI-related competencies becoming important

compliance_calendar.annual_review: IEP reviewed each year; must be current at beginning of each school year
compliance_calendar.federal_meeting_notice: At least 7 days written notice required for any IEP meeting
compliance_calendar.evaluation_timeline: 45 school days to complete evaluations and hold eligibility meeting after consent form signed
compliance_calendar.service_implementation: IEP started as soon as possible but no later than 30 calendar days after child qualified for special education
compliance_calendar.triennial_evaluations: New evaluations at least every 3 years
compliance_calendar.ape_specialist_role: Write or modify IEPs; write reports to summarize student performance, social growth, physical development; review APE programs/practices to ensure compliance

error_patterns.iep_documentation_requirements: Must include summary of present level of performance in PE content, frequency and duration (minutes and days per week), goals, objectives, description of student's physical development per Section 200.1(kk)
error_patterns.critical_compliance_issue: Adapted PE is NOT a related service; OT and PT cannot substitute for physical education
common_errors: Failure to provide parents and specialists with copies of progress report
Special education teachers not setting up timely IEP meetings involving classroom teachers, district reps, student's parents/guardians
Not being able to keep up or meet goal deadlines
Failure to inform parents about any IEP changes
